Preview the additions to items already on Wikidata

Source: R/wikidata_updates.R
preview_wikidata_updates.Rd

The second set of QuickStatements next to [preview_wikidata_export()]: that one creates the items that are missing, this one adds to the items that exist every statement of the model they do not carry - a statement the model gained after the item was created, or a value the register learned later. Nothing is sent.

Usage

preview_wikidata_updates(
  dir = "../register",
  out_dir = ".",
  log_file = NULL,
  records = NULL,
  method = c("search", "sparql"),
  origin = TRUE
)

Arguments

dir

the register repository to read from

out_dir

where to write the batch and the report

log_file

the edit log, to record the batch in and to recognise the export's own items by

records

already-read records, as from [read_register_records()]

method

how to resolve against Wikidata, see [preview_wikidata_export()]

origin

whether to look up who created each item, one request per item

Value

the plan, invisibly: one row per statement to add, to remove, or that differs or is shared, with the item, its origin and creator, the property, the proposed and the current value, the action and the command

Details

A statement whose property the item already carries with another value is a difference, listed in the report but not in the batch: on Wikidata it would become a second value rather than a correction. Statements the export wrote itself are the exception: when their only references point into the register and the model no longer produces their value, the batch removes them, before it adds anything, so a corrected value takes the place of the wrong one. One the export wrote together with somebody else is reported as `"shared"` and left alone. See [wikidata_missing_statements()].

Each item is marked with where it came from. `"codecheck export"` is an item a batch in the edit log created, so the additions finish the export's own work; `"quickstatements"` is one created by a batch the log does not record, and `"other"` one somebody created otherwise - by hand, or by an import of the publisher's metadata. Those are shared items, and the additions to them are worth a look before they are pasted.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
preview_wikidata_updates("../register", out_dir = "wikidata",
                         log_file = "wikidata/wikibase-log.csv")
} # }
